Conference men's basketball season|2019]]) * [[McDonald's All-American Game|McDonald's All-American]] ([[2018 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|2018]]) }} '''Moses Shirief-Lamar Brown''' (born October 13, 1999) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Guangzhou Loong Lions]] of the [[Chinese Basketball Association]] (CBA). A {{convert|7|ft|2|in|adj=on}} [[center (basketball)|center]], Brown was named a [[McDonald's All-American]] as a high school senior in 2018, and in his only [[college basketball|collegiate]] year playing for the [[UCLA Bruins men's basketball|UCLA Bruins]], he was voted to the all-freshman team in the [[Pac-12 Conference men's basketball|Pac-12 Conference]]. After going [[List of National Basketball Association undrafted players|undrafted]] in the [[2019 NBA draft]], Brown spent his rookie season on a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Portland Trail Blazers]]. He has also played for the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]], [[Cleveland Cavaliers]], [[Los Angeles Clippers]], [[Brooklyn Nets]], [[Indiana Pacers]], and [[Dallas Mavericks]]. ==Early life== Brown was born in [[New York City]] to Malcolm Brown and Wanda Williams.{{cite news|title=Moses Brown|work=UCLABruins.com|url=https://uclabruins.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=8194|access-date=August 16, 2018}} His father Malcolm was a {{convert|6|ft|7|in|adj=on}} center in [[junior college]].{{cite news|last=Bolch|first=Ben|title=More than 50 years later, UCLA's Moses Brown stirs up memories of another dominant big man from New York|date=November 21, 2018|newspaper=Los Angeles Times|url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/ucla/la-sp-ucla-basketball-brown-20181121-story.html|access-date=November 22, 2018}} Brown attended [[Archbishop Molloy High School]] in [[Queens]], arriving with limited fanfare as a {{convert|6|ft|8|in|adj=on}} freshman. He was promoted to [[varsity team|varsity]] in his second year, and flourished after growing {{convert|6|in|cm}} and {{convert|100|lb}}. In his junior year, he led Molloy to the [[Catholic High School Athletic Association]] (CHSAA) finals, where the Stanners lost 64–62 in an upset by [[Cardinal Hayes High School|Cardinal Hayes]].{{cite news|last=Barca|first=Christopher|title=Moses Brown named to All-American squad|date=February 8, 2018|newspaper=Queens Chronicle|url=http://www.qchron.com/editions/queenswide/moses-brown-named-to-all-american-squad/article_326e6122-e16f-5f7f-9ce8-394ee9dee653.html}} As a senior, Brown and junior guard [[Cole Anthony]], son of former [[National Basketball Association|NBA]] first-round [[NBA draft|draft]] pick [[Greg Anthony]], formed one of the top duos in all of high school basketball, as well as in Molloy's history.{{cite news|last=Engel|first=Matt|title=Moses Brown, Cole Anthony give Archbishop Molloy highest expectations|date=January 26, 2018|newspaper=Daily News|location=New York|url=http://www.nydailynews.com/sports/more-sports/brown-anthony-give-archbishop-molloy-highest-expectations-article-1.3780309}}{{cite news|title=Cole Anthony & Moses Brown Are The Best Duo in HS Basketball|date=December 14, 2017|work=Slam|url=https://www.slamonline.com/college-hs/high-school/cole-anthony-moses-brown-make-archbishop-molloy-hs-must-see-tv/}} They led the school to the CHSAA's semifinals.{{cite news|last=Thomson|first=Josh|title=Boys basketball: R.J. Davis, Alan Griffin team for 64 points as Stepinac earns redemption|date=March 8, 2018|newspaper=The Journal News|url=https://www.lohud.com/story/sports/high-school/lohud-varsity-insider/2018/03/08/boys-basketball-r-j-davis-alan-griffin-team-64-points-stepinac-earns-redemption/396838002/}} Brown was voted the league's [[most valuable player]] (MVP).{{cite news|last=Barca|first=Christopher|title=Moses Brown takes home league MVP|date=March 8, 2018|newspaper=Queens Chronicle|url=http://www.qchron.com/editions/queenswide/moses-brown-takes-home-league-mvp/article_5446ed21-9642-56f2-9dd9-ef081f5fac62.html}} He was named a [[McDonald's All-American]], becoming the school's first player to garner the honor since [[Kenny Anderson (basketball)|Kenny Anderson]] in 1989.{{cite news|last=Braziller|first=Zach|title=Division I recruit blazes trail for New York City talent|date=January 20, 2018|newspaper=The New York Post|url=https://nypost.com/2018/01/20/division-i-recruit-blazes-trail-for-new-york-city-talent/}} Brown earned MVP honors in the [[Ballislife All-American Game]].{{cite news|title=McClung wins slam dunk contest and scores 20 in all-star game|date=May 6, 2018|newspaper=Bristol Herald Courier|url=https://www.heraldcourier.com/sports/mcclung-wins-slam-dunk-contest-and-scores-in-all-star/article_2c3e59e6-50e3-11e8-b814-2f28e0b4b69a.html}} ==College career== Brown chose to play for [[UCLA Bruins men's basketball|UCLA]] over [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky]], [[Maryland Terrapins men's basketball|Maryland]] and [[Florida State Seminoles men's basketball|Florida State]].{{cite news|last=Brzezinski|first=Alec|title=McDonald's All-American Moses Brown commits to UCLA|date=January 22, 2018|work=Sporting News|url=http://www.sportingnews.com/us/ncaa-basketball/news/moses-brown-recruiting-news-ucla-kentucky-maryland-fsu/hkd6lumtbl0r1fg8lf0s6ntzk}} Rated a five-star prospect, he was the top newcomer in the Bruins [[college recruiting|recruiting]] class for [[2018–19 UCLA Bruins men's basketball team|2018–19]] that ranked in the top-10 nationally and also included [[Shareef O'Neal]], son of Hall of Famer [[Shaquille O'Neal]].{{cite news|last=Bolch|first=Ben|title=UCLA announces the signing of Shareef O'Neal, Shaquille's son|date=August 6, 2018|newspaper=Los Angeles Times|url=http://www.latimes.com/sports/ucla/la-sp-ucla-shareef-oneal-20180806-story.html}} Brown provided the Bruins with a replacement at [[center (basketball)|center]] for the graduated [[Thomas Welsh (basketball)|Thomas Welsh]]. Although he stood {{convert|7|ft|1|in|adj=on}}, there was concern that Brown was underweight at {{convert|235|lb}}.{{cite magazine|last=Caron|first=Emily|title=Moses Brown Brings a Different Dimension to a Young and Talented UCLA Team|date=August 13, 2018|magazine=Sports Illustrated|url=https://www.si.com/college-basketball/2018/08/13/ucla-bruins-recruiting-moses-brown}} UCLA coach [[Steve Alford]] believed that he might still be growing and had "his best basketball ahead of him."{{cite news|last=Nguyen|first=Thuc Nhi|title=UCLA basketball signs Moses Brown, Tyger Campbell, waits for final piece of recruiting class|date=April 12, 2018|newspaper=Los Angeles Daily News|url=https://www.dailynews.com/2018/04/11/ucla-basketball-signs-moses-brown-tyger-campbell-waits-for-final-piece-of-recruiting-class/}} Brown was inconsistent as a freshman, dominating some games while being a nonfactor in others.{{cite news|last=Bolch|first=Ben|title=UCLA's Moses Brown won't play against Utah because of conduct violation|date=March 9, 2019|newspaper=Los Angeles Times|url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/ucla/la-sp-ucla-brown-20190309-story.html|access-date=March 11, 2019}} In the season opener, he scored 19 points on 9-of-10 shooting, including five [[slam dunk]]s, and had 17 [[rebound (basketball)|rebounds]] in a 96–71 win over [[Purdue Fort Wayne Mastodons men's basketball|Purdue Fort Wayne]].{{cite news|last=Hernandez|first=Dylan|title=Moses Brown is one big reason to watch UCLA basketball|date=November 7, 2018|newspaper=Los Angeles Times|url=http://www.latimes.com/sports/ucla/la-sp-ucla-basketball-hernandez-20181107-story.html|access-date=November 13, 2018}} He was the first UCLA player to have 19 points and 17 rebounds in his college debut since Lew Alcindor, known later as [[Kareem Abdul-Jabbar]].{{efn|Alcindor had 56 points and 21 rebounds as a sophomore against [[USC Trojans men's basketball|USC]] on December 3, [[1966–67 UCLA Bruins men's basketball team|1966]]. At the time, freshman were ineligible to play varsity.{{cite news|last=Alexander|first=Jim|title=Alexander: UCLA freshman Moses Brown is already tough to play against|date=November 17, 2018|newspaper=The Press-Enterprise|url=https://www.ocregister.com/2018/11/17/alexander-ucla-freshman-moses-brown-is-already-tough-to-play-against/|access-date=November 19, 2018|via=OCRegister.com}}}} On November 16, 2018, Brown had 23 points and 14 rebounds in a 95–58 win over [[Saint Francis Red Flash men's basketball|Saint Francis]] to become the first UCLA freshman to record a [[double-double]] in his first three games. He nearly had a [[triple-double]] with eight [[block (basketball)|blocks]] in 29 minutes, having left the game for good with around six minutes remaining.{{cite news|last=Bolch|first=Ben|title=UCLA sizzles in second half to blow out St. Francis 95–58|date=November 16, 2018|newspaper=Los Angeles Times|url=http://www.latimes.com/sports/ucla/la-sp-ucla-st-francis-20181116-story.html|access-date=November 19, 2018}} After facing smaller post players from small-program schools, Brown struggled offensively against [[Nick Ward (basketball)|Nick Ward]] of No. 11 [[Michigan State Spartans men's basketball|Michigan State]] with only five points, 10 rebounds and three blocks in an 87–67 loss to the Spartans in the [[Las Vegas Invitational (basketball)|Las Vegas Invitational]].{{cite news|last=Nguyen|first=Thuc Nhi|title=Michigan State crushes UCLA men's basketball in Las Vegas Invitational|date=November 22, 2018|newspaper=Los Angeles Daily News|url=https://www.dailynews.com/2018/11/22/michigan-state-crushes-ucla-mens-basketball-in-las-vegas-invitational/|access-date=November 24, 2018}} In the consolation game, UCLA dropped its second straight contest to a top-15 team, losing to No. 7 [[North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball|North Carolina]] as Brown played just eight minutes before fouling out.{{cite news|last=Nguyen|first=Thuc Nhi|title=UCLA men's basketball fades in second half in loss to North Carolina|date=November 23, 2018|newspaper=Los Angeles Daily News|url=https://www.dailynews.com/2018/11/23/ucla-mens-basketball-fades-in-second-half-in-loss-to-north-carolina/|access-date=November 24, 2018}} On December 2, he had 12 points, 10 rebounds, and three blocks in an 82–58 win over [[Loyola Marymount Lions men's basketball|Loyola Marymount]]. It was his first double-double since the third game of the season, and it came in his first matchup against a fellow 7-footer, the Lions' {{convert|7|ft|3|in|adj=on}} Mattias Markusson.{{cite news|last=Bolch|first=Ben|title=UCLA fires on all cylinders, rout Loyola Marymount 82–58|date=December 2, 2018|newspaper=Los Angeles Times|url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/ucla/la-sp-ucla-lmu-20181202-story.html|access-date=December 3, 2018}}{{cite news|last=Nguyen|first=Thuc Nhi|title=UCLA men's basketball hands Loyola Marymount its first loss|date=December 2, 2018|newspaper=Los Angeles Daily News|url=https://www.dailynews.com/2018/12/02/ucla-mens-basketball-hands-loyola-marymount-its-first-loss/|access-date=December 3, 2018}} On January 26, 2019, Brown snapped out of a two-week slump with 11 points, 15 rebounds and two blocks to help the Bruins end a three-game losing streak in a 90–69 win over [[Arizona Wildcats men's basketball|Arizona]].{{cite news|last=Bolch|first=Ben|title=UCLA's Moses Brown comes up big in 90–69 rout over Arizona|date=January 26, 2019|newspaper=Los Angeles Times|url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/ucla/la-sp-ucla-arizona-20190126-story.html|access-date=January 29, 2019}} He missed the regular season finale against [[Utah Utes men's basketball|Utah]] due to an unspecified violation of the school's student-athlete code of conduct. Brown finished the season averaging 9.7 points and a team-leading 8.3 rebounds, and ranked fourth in the [[Pac-12 Conference men's basketball|Pac-12 Conference]] with 1.9 blocks per game.{{cite news|last=Bolch|first=Ben|title=Moses Brown is leaving UCLA after one season to enter the NBA draft|date=April 23, 2019|newspaper=Los Angeles Times|url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/ucla/la-sp-moses-brown-ucla-nba-20190423-story.html|access-date=May 8, 2019}} He was named to the Pac-12 All-Freshman Team and was an honorable mention for the conference's all-defensive team.{{cite press release|url=https://pac-12.com/article/2019/03/11/pac-12-announces-2018-19-mens-basketball-annual-major-awards |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190330225745/https://pac-12.com/article/2019/03/11/pac-12-announces-2018-19-mens-basketball-annual-major-awards |url-status=dead |archive-date=March 30, 2019 |title=Pac-12 announces 2018–19 Men's Basketball annual major awards |publisher=[[Pac-12 Conference]] |date=March 11, 2019 |access-date=March 11, 2019}} After the season, he [[NBA draft declaration|declared for the NBA draft]].{{cite news|last=Nguyen|first=Thuc Nhi|title=Freshman Moses Brown leaves UCLA basketball for NBA draft|date=April 23, 2019|newspaper=Los Angeles Daily News|url=https://www.dailynews.com/2019/04/23/freshman-moses-brown-leaves-ucla-basketball-for-nba-draft/|access-date=May 8, 2019}} ==Professional career== ===Portland Trail Blazers / Texas Legends (2019–2020)=== Brown went [[List of National Basketball Association undrafted players|undrafted]] in the [[2019 NBA draft]].{{cite news|first=Thuc Nhi|last=Nguyen|title=UCLA's Jaylen Hands headed to Brooklyn Nets after going 56th in NBA draft|url=https://www.dailynews.com/2019/06/20/uclas-jaylen-hands-headed-to-brooklyn-nets-after-going-56th-in-nba-draft/|newspaper=Los Angeles Daily News|date=June 20, 2019|access-date=June 22, 2019}} He joined the [[Houston Rockets]] for the [[2019 NBA Summer League]],{{cite news|first=Reid|last=Laymance|title=Rockets set Summer League roster|url=https://www.chron.com/sports/rockets/article/Rockets-set-Summer-League-roster-14064001.php|newspaper=Houston Chronicle|date=July 1, 2019|access-date=July 4, 2019}} playing briefly in one game.{{cite news|first=Austin|last=Kent|title=BLAZERS SIGN MOSES BROWN TO TRAINING CAMP DEAL|url=https://www.slamonline.com/nba/blazers-sign-moses-brown-to-training-camp-deal/|website=SlamOnline.com|date=September 9, 2019|access-date=October 2, 2019}} On September 9, 2019, Brown signed a training camp contract with the [[Portland Trail Blazers]].{{cite tweet|first=Adrian|last=Wojnarowski|title=UCLA center Moses Brown has signed a training camp deal with Portland, league source tells ESPN.|number=1171107619538374656|user=wojespn|date=September 9, 2019|access-date=July 13, 2025}}{{cite web|title=TRAIL BLAZERS SIGN THREE PLAYERS, ANNOUNCE TRAINING CAMP ROSTER|url=https://www.nba.com/blazers/news/2019/9/12/blazers-announce-training-camp-roster|website=NBA.com|date=September 12, 2019|access-date=September 13, 2019}} He played in all five preseason games, averaging 5.2 points, 2.2 rebounds and 1.0 blocks in 6.9 minutes. On October 18, the Trail Blazers converted his deal into a [[two-way contract]].{{cite web|title=TRAIL BLAZERS CONVERT MOSES BROWN TO TWO-WAY CONTRACT|url=https://www.nba.com/blazers/news/2018/10/18/blazers-convert-moses-brown-to-two-way|website=NBA.com|date=October 18, 2019|access-date=October 29, 2019}} On October 27, they assigned him to the [[Texas Legends]] of the [[NBA G League]].{{cite web|title=TRAIL BLAZERS TRANSFER MOSES BROWN AND JAYLEN HOARD TO TEXAS LEGENDS|url=https://www.nba.com/blazers/news/2019/10/27/blazers-transfer-moses-brown-jaylen-hoard-to-texas-legends|website=NBA.com|date=October 27, 2019|access-date=October 27, 2019}} He was transferred back to Portland on November 9 amid multiple injuries to their frontcourt, including centers [[Pau Gasol]] and [[Jusuf Nurkić]].{{cite news|first=Jamie|last=Goldberg|title=Moses Brown, Jaylen Hoard transferred to Portland Trail Blazers|url=https://www.oregonlive.com/blazers/2019/11/moses-brown-jaylen-hoard-transferred-to-portland-trail-blazers.html|newspaper=The Oregonian|date=November 9, 2019|access-date=November 13, 2019}} Brown was sent to the G League on January 26, 2020.{{cite news|title=Trail Blazers' Moses Brown: Sent to G League|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/trail-blazers-moses-brown-sent-to-g-league/|website=CBSSports.com|date=January 26, 2020|access-date=May 28, 2020}} On February 29, Brown posted a career-high 25 points and 10 rebounds for Texas in a win over the [[Northern Arizona Suns]].{{cite news|title=Trail Blazers' Moses Brown: Posts another big line Saturday|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/trail-blazers-moses-brown-posts-another-big-line-saturday/|website=CBSSports.com|date=March 1, 2020|access-date=May 28, 2020}}{{cite web|title=Payne and Brown Post Career Nights in Texas' Win Over Suns|url=https://texas.gleague.nba.com/news/payne-and-brown-post-career-nights-in-texas-win-over-suns/|website=NBA.com|date=March 1, 2020|access-date=December 25, 2020}}{{Dead link|date=January 2026 |bot=InternetArchiveBot }} He appeared in nine total games for Portland, while playing in 30 for Texas and averaging 14.4 points on a team-high 64.1 [[field goal percentage]] in 19.4 minutes with team-highs of 7.7 rebounds and 1.3 blocks per game.{{cite web|title=Thunder Signs Moses Brown and Josh Hall to Two-Way Contracts|url=https://www.nba.com/thunder/news/brown-hall-201209|website=NBA.com|date=December 9, 2020|access-date=December 9, 2020}} ===Oklahoma City Thunder / Blue (2020–2021)=== On December 9, 2020, Brown signed a two-way contract with the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]]. He played in the G League with the [[Oklahoma City Blue]]. For the week ending February 23, 2021, he was voted the G League Player of the Week after leading the Blue to a 5–0 record while averaging 19.8 points, 15.0 rebounds, 2.3 blocks and 1.3 [[steal (basketball)|steals]] per game.{{cite news|first=Logan|last=Newman|title=Moses Brown named to All-NBA G League First Team, Defensive Team|url=https://okcthunderwire.usatoday.com/2021/03/23/moses-brown-all-nba-g-league-first-team-defensive-team/|newspaper=USA Today|date=March 23, 2021|access-date=March 24, 2021}} He was named to the [[All-NBA G League First Team]] after season averages of 18.5 points, 13.9 rebounds and 1.9 blocks in 26.4 minutes per game.{{cite news|first=Logan|last=Newman|title=5 takeaways: Thunder fall to Knicks as Lu Dort takes ball handling duties|url=https://okcthunderwire.usatoday.com/lists/5-takeaways-thunder-lose-to-knicks-lu-dort-moses-brown/|newspaper=USA Today|date=March 13, 2021|access-date=March 16, 2021}} He was also placed on the NBA G League All-Defensive Team. On March 14, Brown made his first career start for the Thunder, replacing a resting [[Al Horford]] in a game against the [[Memphis Grizzlies]].{{cite web|title=Thunder's Moses Brown: Set for first career start|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/thunders-moses-brown-set-for-first-career-start/|website=CBSSports.com|date=March 14, 2021|access-date=March 14, 2021}} In his second consecutive start on March 16 against the [[Chicago Bulls]], he had 20 points and 16 rebounds for his first career double-double, which he already notched by halftime with 14 points and 10 rebounds. It was his fourth straight game setting a career high in points, which set a Thunder team record. He also had five blocks to become just the second player in team history to record 20+ points, 15+ rebounds and 5+ blocks in a game.{{cite news|first=Logan|last=Newman|title=Thunder center Moses Brown has double-double at halftime vs. Bulls|url=https://okcthunderwire.usatoday.com/2021/03/16/thunder-moses-brown-double-double-halftime-vs-bulls/|newspaper=USA Today|date=March 16, 2021|access-date=March 25, 2021}}{{cite web|first=Paris|last=Lawson|title=A Tale of Two-Halves in the Windy City|url=https://www.nba.com/thunder/recap/bulls-210316|website=NBA.com|date=March 16, 2021|access-date=March 25, 2021}} On March 27, Oklahoma City announced that Horford would sit out the rest of the season as the team prioritized developing its younger players.{{cite news|first=Joe|last=Mussatto|title=Thunder's Al Horford to sit out rest of season|url=https://www.oklahoman.com/story/sports/nba/thunder/2021/03/27/thunder-center-al-horford-sit-out-rest-season/7032718002/|newspaper=Oklahoman|date=March 27, 2021|access-date=March 31, 2021}} That evening, Brown had career-highs of 21 points and 23 rebounds in a loss to the [[Boston Celtics]]. The rebounds tied a team record set by [[Steven Adams]] in 2018, and his 19 rebounds by halftime set a team record for rebounds in a half. Brown had the second-fastest double-double in Thunder history (8 minutes, 11 seconds).{{cite news|first=Joe|last=Mussatto|title=Brown makes Thunder history in loss to Celtics|url=https://www.oklahoman.com/story/sports/nba/thunder/2021/03/27/okc-thunder-vs-boston-celtics-game-recap-march-27/7034751002/|newspaper=Oklahoman|date=March 27, 2021|access-date=March 30, 2021}}{{cite news|first=Logan|last=Newman|title=Moses Brown matches Dwight Howard, Steven Adams in performance vs. Celtics|url=https://okcthunderwire.usatoday.com/2021/03/28/moses-brown-matches-dwight-howard-steven-adams-in-performance-vs-celtics/|newspaper=USA Today|date=March 28, 2021|access-date=March 30, 2021}} The following day, the Thunder announced that they had signed Brown to a multi-year, standard NBA contract.{{cite web|title=Thunder Signs Moses Brown to Multi-Year Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/thunder/news/brown-210328|website=NBA.com|date=March 28, 2021|access-date=March 28, 2021}} He had been averaging 12.4 points, 12.3 rebounds and 1.6 blocks in 27.7 minutes per game since returning from the G League.{{cite news|first=Logan|last=Newman|title=Moses Brown signs multi-year contract with Thunder|url=https://okcthunderwire.usatoday.com/2021/03/29/moses-brown-signs-contract-with-thunder/|newspaper=USA Today|date=March 29, 2021|access-date=March 30, 2021}} In the season finale against the [[Los Angeles Clippers]], he had career-highs of 24 points and seven blocks, while also adding 18 rebounds.{{cite news|first=Curtis|last=Burkhardt|title=Moses Brown has career night for OKC to help Blazers avoid the Clippers|url=https://www.nbcsports.com/northwest/trail-blazers/moses-brown-has-career-night-okc-help-blazers-avoid-clippers|website=NBCSports.com|date=May 17, 2021|access-date=May 18, 2021}} He ended the season with averages of 8.6 points and 8.9 rebounds.{{cite news|first=Cliff|last=Brunt|title=Strange losing season finally over for Oklahoma
